blocks.label: Survive a knockout hit but be marked to faint later

The survival really happens only for a real hit, not for a damage preview
blocks.packageReason: PACKAGE, written reason: the survive rule (clauses 1 to 4) is inherited from PreFaintReviveAbAttr (B11), whose canApply is not mine to split, and the effect (a STURDY tag that the damage pipeline reads, plus a per-switch-in marker that the matching end-of-turn attr reads) has no library effect: there is no 'survive a lethal hit' block and no 'set a marker' block. Requests R1 (split the inherited canApply into a swappable 'the hit would knock me out' condition) and R2 (effect: survive a knockout at 1 HP) in requests/B17.md. Typed params: none exist; the only number in the chain is the inherited HP rule threshold 0, which is always true. Users: Lingering Musk (6084, attr 2) only; its attr 3 is LingeringMuskPostTurnAbAttr. SUSPECTED GAME BUG, NOT FIXED: this class's apply sets tempSummonData.lingeringMuskFaint = true without checking `simulated`. PreDefendFullHpEndureAbAttr is dispatched from Pokemon.getAttackDamage with the caller's `simulated` flag, and getAttackDamage(simulated: true) is called for damage previews (move-phase.ts:682 and move-effect-phase.ts:1071 target ordering, the enemy move scoring in pokemon.ts around lines 10040 to 10360). A previewed knockout of a Lingering Musk holder (damage >= hp) therefore sets the marker although no hit landed, and the holder faints at the end of the turn. Needs a check by the owner; the declaration records simulated: ignores.

blocks.packageReason: Tier B with a PACKAGE effect. Written reason: the effect is one damageAndUpdate(attacker.hp, INDIRECT) call, but no library effect 'knock out another Pokemon / take all of its remaining HP' exists (request R7 in requests/B17.md); recoil and drain scale with a damage or max-HP share and apply to the holder or the damage dealt, not 'all current HP of the other Pokemon'. The trigger (when I faint) and the one real condition (the knocker is not an ally) are separate blocks. The three guards (a move, a known attacker, still standing) have no registry ids (request R8), so they are written as feasibility; they run first, in the original order, before the gate. The condition used to be `!attacker.getAllies().includes(pokemon)`: getAllies() lists the OTHER ACTIVE battlers on the attacker's side, the atom side.is(ally) compares isPlayer() and identity. They differ only if the knocker is on my side but I am no longer in the field array (not reachable: the faint dispatch runs while I am still on the field). The L1 grid never sets a same-side attacker, so test/tests/elite-redux/decomp/B17/gates.test.ts checks both directions with stand-ins (the old canApply, the refactor, the rebuild and a deliberately wrong gate), and mutual-destruction.test.ts runs the foe direction in a real battle. A real double battle for the ally direction is not possible here: the existing innards-out.test.ts double case also times out in this checkout. Users: Mutual Destruction (6104, attr 0) only. The ability also carries the ability-level flag bypassFaint (set in wireBernerdRosterAbility, not an attr), which belongs to the ability blueprint, not to this block. The ability text mentions Pain Split first; the code deals the attacker's whole current HP directly (the comment in apply says that equals the Pain Split plus Innards Out result), so no Pain Split step exists in this attr. No game bug found.

blocks.packageReason: Tier B (the gate runs through gatedCanApply inside apply, see the header) with a PACKAGE effect. Written reason: the effect writes two string markers in the ER provenance memory (battleData 'oracle:first-entry', summonData 'oracle:guard:N'), and a closure of ANOTHER attr (ReceivedMoveDamageMultiplierAbAttr in Oracle, bound legacy in the precedents) reads them back by string prefix; there is no library effect to set a typed marker (request R9) and no atom to read it (request R3). The number of turns is the typed `guardTurns` setting (1 to 10; the class itself accepts any number, 0 or less would start an already-expired guard). The gate binding is legacy-closure-pending-request R3, so the rebuild is skipped by L2. Users: Oracle (6047, attr 1) only. Oddity, not changed: the ability text says incoming attacks are 'treated as not very effective', but the damage attr halves the damage (x0.5), which is what the guard does in code. Replacing an existing guard marker means a second entry in the same battle never restarts the guard (the first-entry memory blocks it).

The gate binding is legacy-closure-pending-request R3. Users: Oracle (6047, attr 2) only.
